archetype.name: Pretender (puck-starved)
archetype.definition: A .500 team whose record is held up by a hot 5-on-5 PDO and a decent power play while it gets outshot and out-chanced more than almost anyone in the league.

report.headline: A .500 record built on borrowed percentages, with the penalty kill bleeding goals
report.take:
Seattle is 10-9-1 with 21 standings points, third in a Pacific Division where most of the teams are under water. That looks like a team hanging around a playoff spot. The site ranks the Kraken 30th of 32, though, and the underlying numbers explain why. At 5-on-5 they own a 42% CF %, last in the league, and a 45.2% xGF %, 28th. This is a team without the puck, and it was nearly as bad last season, when it posted a 45% CF % on the way to 79 points and a 31st-place site rank. Nothing about the shape of this club is new.

The record is close to even because two things have masked the territorial deficit. The first is a 102.6 PDO at 5-on-5, well above the 100 average, so the even-strength goals have gone in at a rate the chances don't support. The second is a power play converting 23.8%, 11th in the league. Together they produce 3.35 goals a game, 12th, which is respectable for a team that rarely has the puck. The record isn't propped up by close-game luck, either. Pts vs Goal Diff is -0.1, so the 21 points match a -4 goal differential almost exactly. The trouble is that the differential itself leans on percentages.

The penalty kill is the wound. At 60.7% it is last in the league by a distance, against a league average of 77.2%, and it is far worse than any of the last five seasons, which ranged from 72.2% to 78.8%. Some of that should come back toward normal, because a kill this bad is partly bad bounces. The goaltending isn't helping. Philipp Grubauer has been roughly average (.894, +0.4 GSAx). Joey Daccord has been a problem across nine starts (.872, -3.6 GSAx), which pulls the team to -2 GSAx and a D+ grade. One note on the sheet: it lists only a single forward, Jani Nyman, who has four scoreless games, so the F forward grade and the near-zero all-situations shooting figures reflect a thin listing rather than the real attack.

The direction is the worry. October was an 8-6 month with 3.71 goals each way. November is 2-4 at 2.5 scored and 3.17 allowed, and the last five games are 1-4 with a -5 differential. The scoring has come down toward what the shot share suggests, and the goals against haven't improved to make up for it. The 86-point pace assumes the October version keeps showing up. The process says it won't.

strengths.title: A power play that cashes in
strengths.body: At 23.8% the power play sits 11th and above the 22.5% league average. It is the main reason a team this short of 5-on-5 possession still scores at a top-half rate. Conversion rates move around, but it also beat the league norm in past seasons only rarely, so treat it as useful rather than bankable.

strengths.title: Opposing defensemen kept quiet
strengths.body: The defense allows opposing defensemen 0.3 points a game, 4th best in the league and under what those players normally produce. Blueliners account for only 18.8% of the points scored against Seattle, against a 29.3% league norm. Point shots and activating defensemen aren't how teams are beating the Kraken.

strengths.title: Grubauer as a steady option
strengths.body: Philipp Grubauer is at .894 with +0.4 GSAx over 11 starts and sits 27th of 72 on the goalie tab. That is average goaltending, which is exactly what this team needs from its starter. Leaning on him over Daccord is the easiest lever available.

concerns.title: Worst penalty kill in the league
concerns.body: A 60.7% PK ranks 32nd of 32, far below the 77.2% league average. It is also well below every season in the recent history, the lowest of which was 72.2% last year. Part of it is goaltending and part is randomness, so it should rise. Even a rebound to last year's level would still leave it a liability.

concerns.title: Outshot and out-chanced at even strength
concerns.body: Seattle has the lowest CF % in the league at 42% and a 45.2% xGF % that ranks 28th. A 102.6 PDO is covering for it, and percentages that high tend to drift back toward 100. When they do, the goal differential will look like the shot share. The trend matches last season's 45% CF %, so this is structural rather than a slump.

concerns.title: Wingers run free, Daccord leaks
concerns.body: Opposing wingers score 0.95 points a game against Seattle, 30th in the league. They take 59.4% of the points against the Kraken, versus a 43% league share, which points to coverage breakdowns on the flanks. Joey Daccord's -3.6 GSAx in nine starts compounds it, dragging the team's goaltending to a D+.

trend.note: An 8-6 October with even 3.71-3.71 scoring gave way to a 2-4 November at 2.5 goals a game. The last five are 1-4 with a -5 differential, as the offense sinks toward what the shot share supports.

weekAhead.headline: Two soft home games, then an Edmonton back-to-back
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with Anaheim and Chicago at home, a real chance to stop the slide. Chicago is 31st on the site with a -1.33 Goal Diff / GP and a 42.5% xGF %, the rare opponent Seattle might not be badly outplayed by. Anaheim is the trickier one despite its 11-12-1 record. The Ducks have the league's best power play at 34.2%, which is the worst possible matchup for a 60.7% kill. Their goaltending, though, is last in the league by save % and carries -10.7 GSAx, so Seattle's attack should find the net.

The weekend is a home-and-home with Edmonton, 17-5-4 and 7th on the site. The Oilers score heavily (offense rank 3) and run the second-best power play at 32.6%, behind an A- goaltending group. Their 46.5% xGF % and 103.3 PDO suggest they are beatable at 5-on-5. Seattle's discipline will decide whether that matters. Splitting the first two and stealing one from Edmonton would count as a good week.

keyMatchups.title: Ducks power play vs Seattle kill
keyMatchups.body: Anaheim converts 34.2% of its chances, 1st in the league, and Seattle kills 60.7%, 32nd. Every Kraken penalty in this game is close to a coin flip on a goal against. Staying out of the box matters more than anything Seattle does at 5-on-5.

keyMatchups.title: Shooting on shaky Ducks, Hawks goalies
keyMatchups.body: Anaheim's .858 save % is last in the league with -10.7 GSAx, and Chicago's goalies sit at -9.1 GSAx. These are the two best scoring chances Seattle's power play and finishers will get all month. Both games are home dates, which helps.

keyMatchups.title: Edmonton's record runs ahead of play
keyMatchups.body: The Oilers' 46.5% xGF % ranks 25th, and their 2.2 Pts vs Goal Diff is 7th, so they have been winning more than their 5-on-5 play earns. Their offense still ranks 3rd and their power play 2nd. Seattle's path is to keep the games at even strength and lean on Grubauer.

weekAhead.watch: Seattle's penalty count against Anaheim and Edmonton, two top-two power plays facing the league's worst kill.

restOfSeason.body:
The 86-point pace rests on an October the underlying numbers don't back. With the worst CF % in the league, a 28th-ranked xGF % and a 5-on-5 PDO of 102.6, the likeliest path is that even-strength scoring keeps cooling and the goal differential slides further negative. That would leave the Kraken in roughly the high-70s range they have lived in for three straight seasons. Two things can push back. The penalty kill can't stay at 60.7%, and normal regression there will recover some goals. A goaltending split tilted toward Grubauer would also help.

The Pacific gives them some room, since San Jose, Anaheim and Calgary are all below .500. Third place is not out of the question, but a team this short of the puck shouldn't be expected to hold it. Expect something in the 74-84 point range, with the power play carrying more of the offense than it can reliably sustain.
swingFactors: Penalty kill regression toward the league norm
Grubauer vs Daccord share of starts
Whether the 5-on-5 PDO holds as shot share stays last

confidence.note: 20 games is a modest sample, but the possession gap is extreme and matches last season; the roster listing is thin.
